Fixed upstream in models.dev: https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev/pull/3331

Kimi K3 locks sampling server-side (`temperature` fixed at 1.0; other values → HTTP 400). The catalog had advertised `temperature = true`, so clients sent the field and OpenCode Go rejected the request.

#3331 marks the base model `temperature = false` so clients omit it. After catalog refresh, subagent calls that were injecting temperature should stop 400ing.

Related incomplete fix attempt: https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev/pull/3328 (closed as superseded).

Looking forward to this being merged — it will solve a lot of the pain points I encounter when working on multiple features in parallel. It would be great to manage branches natively instead of relying on skills/plugins to orchestrate the workflow.

There is overlap in the underlying Bun `bun:ffi` extraction bug, but this issue is specifically tracking a V2 CLI regression that substantially amplifies it: OpenTUI is initialized before command dispatch even for `--version`, `--help`, `service status`, and `api`.

The current stable V1 release provides a useful control:

- V1 `1.18.3` does not extract OpenTUI for `--version`, `run --help`, `serve --help`, `debug paths`, or a live headless server.
- V1 extracts it only when the interactive TUI actually runs.
- V2 `next-15760`, `next-15803`, and `next-15806` extract it for `--version`; `next-15760` also reproduces it for every tested API and service command.

So this is not intended to duplicate the general cleanup/deduplication problem in #28089. The independently actionable OpenCode change is to avoid importing the renderer for commands that cannot render a TUI, as V1 already does. That would eliminate the high-frequency API and diagnostic amplification while the broader Bun fix remains tracked upstream.

#21427 is the closest prior report, but it covered older V1 releases and was automatically closed as stale with a request to open a new issue if the problem remained relevant. I am happy for maintainers to consolidate this if preferred, but I wanted the V2-specific regression and current-version reproduction to remain visible.

Thanks, I reviewed #27370. It concerns the same configuration field, but the behavior and requested outcome are different.

#27370 explicitly reports that new sessions correctly honor `default_agent`; the problem occurs only when resuming a session whose persisted last-used agent differs from the configured default. It requests a policy for whether resumed sessions should restore persisted state or always use the configured default.

This issue reproduces before that policy question arises:

- A brand-new V2 standalone TUI ignores `default_agent`.
- The reproduction uses an isolated `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, all plugins disabled, and the built-in `plan` agent.
- There is no resumed session or persisted last-used agent involved.
- The full TUI starts with `Build`, apparently because it selects the first catalog entry rather than the configured default.
- The same selector behavior occurs when opening an API-created session that already specifies another agent.

So #37225 is about honoring `default_agent` during initial full-TUI selection, while #27370 is about whether a resumed session should override persisted agent state. They may touch adjacent code, but fixing the resume policy described in #27370 would not necessarily fix new-session startup in V2.

This is not a model limit merge bug. The config mixes V1 and V2 fields: V1 uses `agent`, while V2 uses `agents` and `providers`.

The presence of the V1-only `agent` field causes the loader to classify the entire document as V1. During V1 decoding/migration, the V2 `providers` field is treated as an unknown field and ignored, so the provider/model override never reaches the catalog. That also explains why a custom model alias did not appear.

The immediate fix is to use one config generation consistently:

- V2: migrate `agent` to the V2 `agents` shape and keep `providers`.
- V1: keep `agent`, but use the singular `provider` field.

The model overlay itself already merges partial limits correctly. Separately, we should consider rejecting or warning on mixed V1/V2 documents rather than silently dropping fields.

---Distinct manifestation of this same root cause: cross-session bleed, not just single-session revert. Two separate foreground TUI sessions open concurrently, DB-audited via ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db:

- Session A (brave-star) manually switched to plan + omlx/Qwen3.5-9B-OptiQ-4bit, ran on that combo for 8+ turns.
- Went idle ~90s while Session B (crisp-orchid) was actively used with build + llama.cpp/qwen3.6-35b-a3b-mtp.
- Session A's next turn after idling: persisted session.model in the DB had silently flipped to build + llama.cpp/qwen3.6-35b-a3b-mtp — exactly Session B's active selection, not Session A's own default or last-used.

Ruled out config-file involvement: opencode.json mtime predates the incident window by hours, so it isn't the picker writing back to shared config.

This is consistent with @dsy122's syncedSessionID-closure theory, but implies the "already synced" flag (or the local.model store it reads from) isn't scoped per-session at all — it's shared across concurrently open sessions/windows, not just lost on remount within one session. Happy to share full log/DB excerpts if useful.

### Deeper finding while trying to verify end-to-end

I've been trying to prove this patch works end-to-end via a runtime MCP flow (external orchestrator posts \`/mcp\` to add a bot-scoped MCP entry, then hits \`/api/session/:id/prompt\` for Kimi to invoke it). Two independent architecture splits blocked verification, and are worth calling out here — they aren't caused by this patch, but they mean the patch only fixes _half_ of what a runtime-MCP-driven \"force tool call\" flow needs.

**1) Two MCP services, not one.**

- \`packages/opencode/src/mcp/index.ts\` is \`@opencode/MCP\` — the target of the runtime \`POST /mcp\` endpoint. Instance-scoped via \`InstanceState\`.
- \`packages/core/src/mcp/index.ts\` is \`@opencode/v2/MCP\` — what the core \`SessionModelRequest.prepare\` reads. Its \`runtime\` map is initialized from config \`documents\` at layer construction time only (\`index.ts:184-192\`), and I couldn't find a runtime-add code path into it.

Runtime-added MCP entries (via the endpoint from #37308) land in the opencode service, but the SessionRunner uses the core service — so those tools never reach \`registry.materialize\` and never appear in the LLM request's tools list. Verified by watching \`sync-bot-63\` show \"connected\" in the daemon MCP status (queried with the same \`?directory=\`) while Kimi's assistant response enumerated exactly the built-ins (\`read/write/edit/grep/glob/shell/websearch/webfetch/question/skill/subagent/execute\`) with no MCP entry.

**2) Two prompt code paths, not one.**

- \`packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts\` (\`SessionPrompt.prompt\`) — reached by \`POST /session/:id/message\` and \`POST /session/:id/prompt_async\`. This is the file this PR patches.
- \`packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts\` + \`packages/core/src/session/model-request.ts\` (\`SessionRunner\` + \`SessionModelRequest.prepare\`) — reached by \`POST /api/session/:id/prompt\` via \`SessionPending.admit\`.

The second path _also_ hard-codes \`toolChoice\`, at \`model-request.ts:90\`:
\`\`\`ts
toolChoice: stepLimitReached ? \"none\" : undefined,
\`\`\`

So even after this PR lands, orchestrators using the legacy \`/api/session/:id/prompt\` route (which is currently the working streaming path for external clients — the direct v2 endpoints emit a \"share subscriber failed: Expected string, got undefined\" on message.updated and never produce an assistant reply on the current v2-test build) still get \`toolChoice: undefined\`.

**Suggested follow-up scope** (either as a review comment I can address in this PR, or as separate issues):

1. Mirror the same three-way precedence at \`packages/core/src/session/model-request.ts:90\`, threading toolChoice from \`Session.prompt\` (core service) via a new field on \`SessionPending\` through to \`PrepareInput\`.
2. Bridge runtime-added MCP entries from \`@opencode/MCP\` into \`@opencode/v2/MCP\`, so tools registered via #37308's endpoint reach \`SessionModelRequest.prepare.executableTools\`.
3. Fix the v2 direct endpoints' \"Expected string, got undefined\" on message.updated so orchestrators can migrate off the legacy \`/api\` path.

Happy to take any/all of these as follow-up PRs if there's interest, but wanted to flag the shape of it here in case a maintainer already has a preferred design (the runner is under active refactor).

The core PR still stands as-is — it's the correct fix for the direct-endpoint code path, and it's the one this PR's title/description claims.
